title: Define canonical audit event taxonomy and JSON diff format for RBAC v2 / SSO changes
creator: Ava Chen
description: Background: With RBAC v2, expanded admin controls, and SSO/SAML configuration options, we must standardize what we log and how changes are recorded. Inconsistent audit records across API, Console, Dedicated control plane, and Private deployments make investigations slow and automations brittle. Goal: publish a canonical audit event taxonomy and a small, human- and machine-readable diff format for config/compliance events so security, SRE, and product teams can reliably query history, detect policy violations, and feed SIEMs. This ticket defines scope, a proposed event schema, diff encoding rules, retention/PII guidance, and a rollout plan for producers and sinks.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical event schema doc published in Security Confluence and linked from developer-audit-rpc README
Producer libraries (go/java/python/ts) have API surface to emit required fields and canonical diff encoding
At least one service (console-auth, rbac-service) sends events conforming to schema to the audit pipeline (S3->BigQuery/SIEM) in staging
Automated schema validation tests added to CI for producers + contract tests for consumers
Sampling/staging policy and retention plan documented; PII fields flagged and redacted where required
proposed_schema_summary: Top-level fields (all required unless noted): event_id, timestamp_iso, event_type, severity_level, outcome, actor_type, actor_id, actor_display_name, actor_role(s), target_type, target_id, target_display, action, resource_path, request_id, correlation_id, client_ip, user_agent, location, system_tags (optional), before_snapshot (optional), after_snapshot (optional), diff (optional JSON Patch string), metadata (optional freeform key-values). Use stable event_type taxonomy (e.g., auth.login, auth.saml.config_change, rbac.role.create, rbac.role.update, rbac.role.delete, config.secret.rotate, deployment.model.deploy, capacity.scale, api.key.create, console.user.login). All timestamps use RFC3339 / ISO8601 with timezone. actor_type is one of [user, service, system, api_key]. outcome is one of [success, failure, denied].
diff_format_spec: We propose canonicalizing diffs as JSON Patch (RFC 6902) with these constraints: 1) Use 'replace' for value updates, 'add' and 'remove' for structural changes; 2) For arrays of objects (e.g., policy bindings), diffs MUST include identity keys in path segments using an index-like syntax '/bindings[id=123]/roles' to make patches idempotent when applied by human auditors; 3) 'before_snapshot' and 'after_snapshot' include compact projections (only fields from the allowed audit projection list) to make search fast; 4) Diffs must not include raw secrets. If a secret changes, emit a high-level event with field set to "<redacted>" and include a metadata flag secret_changed=true; 5) For RBAC role grants, emit both a high-level rbac.role.grant event and a diff that shows the previous bindings. Producers must create a human-readable summary string in metadata.summary for quick display in Console and Slack alerts. Example encoding provided in examples field. For long diffs (>8 operations) produce a compressed base64 payload and a short summary in metadata.
examples: Example 1 - Role update (human-friendly): {"event_type":"rbac.role.update","timestamp_iso":"2026-03-14T09:21:33Z","actor_type":"user","actor_id":"u_7f9b3","actor_display_name":"Elena Gomez","target_type":"role","target_id":"role_finance_analytics","action":"update","outcome":"success","diff":"[{\"op\":\"replace\",\"path\":\"/permissions/compute/limits\",\"value\":\"increased\"}]","metadata.summary":"Elena updated role_finance_analytics: increased compute limits"}
